note: Fail-first pitfall for purchase-price carry-forward tests in a replay: checking the incoming_state of the SAME gameweek whose current_attributes carries a price rise proves nothing, because that state was threaded from the PRIOR gameweek's decision (built before the rise happened). Needed a 3-round season, not 2, to make the carry-forward test fail against a deliberately broken implementation before it could be trusted. SquadState.bank_tenths is defined as SquadRules.budget_tenths minus the sum of the new squad's purchase prices (carried-forward for held players, current price for new ones). This keeps 'spent + banked == budget' exactly true for every gameweek S6 can construct, ONLY because no transfer accounting exists yet (no hits, no selling-price haircut). S7 must either preserve this invariant when it adds selling-price rules (haircut on price rises means a sale credits LESS than the held purchase price, breaking the invariant unless bank is updated by actual sale proceeds rather than by re-summing purchase prices) or explicitly document that the invariant no longer holds post-S7. Two corroborating details that make the hoist semantically safe: (1) the current per-element rollup input is already filtered to (element==e OR team==t), so it ALREADY contains other players' rows, which are discarded afterwards by rollup.filter(element==e) - proving extra rows in the input cannot perturb element e's own output; (2) the per-(element,round) placeholder row only ever joins its own group.
